# Library and configuration

::: {.doc-lead}
Know what belongs to a project and what is shared across your projects.
:::

Flux's reference system has two layers, and the split is what lets a permanent reading library
coexist with fully self-contained projects:

- **FluxLib** — the machine-global library. One collection of papers for *you*, shared by every
  project on the machine. This is what the [Library](/docs/library.html) workspace manages: every paper
  you save, its PDF, your highlights and notes, tags, collections, reading status.
- **The project's cited subset** — each project carries its own `references/library.bib`
  holding real copies of just the entries it cites. Citing a paper in a manuscript materializes
  its entry from FluxLib into the project.

The point of the split: your library can grow to thousands of papers without bloating any
project, and a project still **zips, clones, and compiles standalone** — hand the folder to a
collaborator and every citation resolves, no FluxLib required.

## The citekey is the join key {#the-citekey-is-the-join-key}

Every paper has one stable **citation key** (`smithNeuralBasis2021`-style — the same format
Zotero's Better BibTeX plugin uses, so keys arriving from a [Zotero
sync](/docs/zotero.html) and keys Flux mints itself look alike). That key is how you cite
it in any manuscript (`[@smithNeuralBasis2021]`), the name of its folder in the library, and
the handle agents use to fetch, highlight, or discuss it. Keys are permanent join keys — they
never change out from under a project.

## What's inside FluxLib {#whats-inside-fluxlib}

FluxLib lives at `<FluxConfig>/FluxLib` (by default `~/FluxConfig/FluxLib`; `flux config`
prints this machine's paths). Like [projects](/docs/projects-and-files.html), it's plain files with a
clear source-vs-derived split:

- `library.bib` — the canonical BibTeX file and the source of truth for your references. Any
  reference manager that reads BibTeX can open it.
- `items/<citekey>/` — everything belonging to one paper: the PDF (or, when Zotero sync runs
  in linked mode, a small pointer file naming the PDF in Zotero's folder), a `supplements/`
  folder for supplementary files, your highlights, and the extracted text that powers
  full-text search.
- `pdfs_to_assign/` — the watched **inbox folder** for PDFs (not the comment [Inbox](/docs/comments.html)): drop PDFs here and Flux identifies each one
  from its own contents and files it under the right paper (refusing, rather than guessing, when
  it isn't sure).
- `.fluxlib/` — derived indexes (search, full-text, enrichment). Rebuildable caches, never the
  truth: delete them and Flux regenerates them from the files above.

## Portability {#portability}

Because it's all files, moving machines is copying a folder: `~/FluxConfig` carries your
library (`FluxLib/`), your agent context and skills (`Context/UserContext/`, including `Skills/`),
and your global plot library (`plot_library/`). Back it up like you'd back up your documents — it *is* documents.
